# Voice and visual briefing (build your own)

Daily "ahead of the day" briefing plus a weekly rewind, each as a short voice memo and a visual player with synced subtitles. You build and run the player yourself, in the owner's own project, on their own machine or their own hosting.

## 0. Reference recipe (read first)
Guides and example code: https://voice-briefing-player.vercel.app/llms.txt . It's a recipe to copy, not a service. Never send the owner's data there.
- Narration: /docs/narration.md . Presentation rules: /docs/presentation.md . Detail brief format: /docs/detail-brief.md . Agent prompt and output files: /template.md
- Example code to copy into your own Next.js project: /code/ (schema.ts templates, compose.ts, reducer.ts, render-tts.ts for single-take TTS + whisper alignment, player components, optional link minting).
- Extra primitive sketches: the "Extend it: more primitives" section of llms.txt.
- Example of the finished result with made-up data: /b/qo2sse3CDMeN7A-zeSloTg
Where the recipe and this summary disagree, follow the recipe.

## 1. First-time setup
- Create a small Next.js project in the owner's workspace (or on their computer), copy the /code/ files in, and add their own TTS API key as a secret.
- Pick how they'll view it (section 7) and test with one sample briefing before the first real one.

## 2. Gather
- Sources: connectors first (mail, calendar, tasks, other bots' notes). For heavy mailboxes keep a local read-only mirror on a schedule.
- Fixed window in the owner's time zone (daily: 09:00 yesterday to 09:00 today; weekly: Mon 00:00 to Sun 18:00). Say the window and message count first.
- Order: busiest topic first; within it new asks, problems, money, logistics. Then calendar, misc, alerts last.
- Cut: keep deadlines, money changes, complaints, approvals, slipping dates. Skip admin noise and newsletters.
- Cites, not vibes: every claim traces to a source. Copy amounts as written, never estimate. Unknown = "to confirm".
- Count check: for every number you say, list the items behind it and check for missing, overlapping and the unique total.

## 3. Outputs per run
Script (one fact per line, blank line between topics), detail brief (tables per topic, dates tied to items, a "not on screen" section), and storyboard JSON (one cue per line, templates from your schema only, atChar timing).

## 4. Narration (summary)
- Calm colleague over coffee: warm, even, unhurried, no drama. Ear-first, conclusion first.
- Newline = short pause, blank line = longer pause. Never rush numbers.
- Don't pre-spell digits; put reading rules in the TTS instructions (quantities natural, ids digit by digit, dates spoken, codes as letters, names in their own language, no symbols aloud). Structure as Voice Affect / Tone / Pacing / Pronunciation / Pauses; short direct traits.
- One TTS take for the whole script (split only at topic breaks if over the limit), then whisper word timestamps aligned back to lines.

## 5. Presentation (summary)
- Status colours: red alert, amber warn, grey info, strikethrough only if the source says cancelled. Max ~6 items on screen, +N for the rest. Everything highlighted is spoken; nothing animates unless spoken.
- Never on screen: bank details, phone numbers, raw emails, internal margins, phishing senders or links.

## 6. Extend the visuals
Start with the built-in templates (hello, item list, calendar, table, bubble). Add primitives to your own schema when a briefing needs them, each driven by spoken cues: map (pins, route, travel time), gauge (progress or budget), line/bar chart (trends, week vs week), stat card with sparkline, checklist that ticks as spoken, mermaid diagram with nodes lighting up, timeline/Gantt (today's schedule, slipping bars), kanban move, weather/commute strip, avatar row (who you're meeting), quote card, countdown. Build each once, add it to the schema, reuse it.

## 7. Running it (owner's choice)
1. Same Wi-Fi, nicest: Vercel Labs portless in LAN mode (`portless proxy start --lan`) for a named .local URL. https://github.com/vercel-labs/portless
2. Same Wi-Fi, simplest: `next start -H 0.0.0.0`, share http://<computer LAN IP>:<port>.
3. Anywhere: deploy the owner's own project to their own Vercel with unguessable, expiring links.
Send the link straight into chat when ready.

## 8. Feedback loop
The owner replies, often by voice. Each correction becomes a memory fact or rule line for next run; re-verify corrected facts against the source.

## 9. Weekly rewind ("Wrapped for your week")
Sunday evening: what got done, biggest win, busiest day, who the owner dealt with most, what slipped, one fun stat, next week. Use stat cards, charts and top-N lists from section 6. Same rules, brighter tone.

# Getting started

I'll build you your own voice briefing each morning and a weekly rewind on Sundays, each with a visual player you can open on your phone. It runs on your own setup, built from your mail and calendar, with every point traced back to a source. Here's an example of what it looks like: https://voice-briefing-player.vercel.app/b/qo2sse3CDMeN7A-zeSloTg

Ask one at a time:
1. What should I cover: work mail, personal mail, calendar, tasks, or something else? Connect anything that isn't connected yet.
2. What time for the morning briefing, and do you want the Sunday rewind too?
3. What language, and how long: about 1 minute or about 3?
4. Where should the player run: your computer on home Wi-Fi (easiest), or your own Vercel so it works anywhere?
5. Ask for a TTS API key through a secret request.

Then read https://voice-briefing-player.vercel.app/llms.txt, set up the project per section 1 of the voice-and-visual-briefing skill, save the answers as memory facts, create the daily and weekly routines, and make the first briefing now. Send the link straight into chat and ask for feedback.
